title: Set 293

sentences.ko: 솔직히 말해도 돼? 색은 너한테 진짜 잘 어울리는데, 어깨가 좀 끼어. 한 치수 큰 게 있으면 나라면 바꾸겠어. 안 그러면 한 2주 입고 안 입게 될 거야.
sentences.text: Honestly? The color's great on you, but it's kind of tight across the shoulders. If they have it one size up, I'd swap it, because otherwise you're going to stop wearing it after like two weeks.

alts.text: Love the color on you, but it's kinda tight in the shoulders. I'd swap it for one size up if they've got it, or you're gonna quit wearing it in like two weeks.

To be honest, the color suits you very well, but it is a little tight across the shoulders. If they have it one size larger, I would exchange it, because otherwise you will stop wearing it after about two weeks.

sentences.note: **tight across the shoulders** 는 옷이 어깨 쪽이 낀다는 말입니다. **one size up** 은 한 치수 큰 것이고, **swap it** 은 산 물건을 다른 것으로 바꾼다는 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: 친구가 산 옷 어떠냐고 물었을 때 솔직하게 말하기

sentences.ko: 이사를 갈까 말까 계속 왔다 갔다 해. 새 집이 회사에서는 더 가까운데 뒷마당이 없어지거든. 그리고 모르겠어, 부엌 짐 쌀 생각만 하면 그냥 1년만 더 살까 싶어.
sentences.text: I keep going back and forth on moving. The new place would be closer to work, but I'd lose the backyard, and I don't know, every time I picture packing up the kitchen I'm like, maybe I'll just stay one more year.

alts.text: Can't decide if I should move. New place is closer to work, but no backyard, and ugh, whenever I think about packing the kitchen I'm like, eh, maybe one more year here.

I keep changing my mind about moving. The new home would be closer to work, but I would lose the backyard, and to be honest, every time I imagine packing up the kitchen, I think that perhaps I will stay one more year.

sentences.note: **going back and forth** 는 이랬다저랬다 마음을 못 정하는 것입니다. **I'm like** 는 말할 때 그 순간 든 생각을 옮기는 표현으로 ~싶다에 가깝습니다.

sentences.ko: 내가 엄청 들떠서 샀던 비싼 블렌더 기억나? 딱 두 번 썼어. 너무 시끄러워서 식구들 일어나기 전에는 아무것도 못 만들어. 그래서 지금은 조리대 반을 차지하고만 있고, 볼 때마다 내가 바보 같아.
sentences.text: Remember that fancy blender I was so excited about? I've used it twice. It's so loud I can't make anything before everybody's awake, so now it just takes up half the counter and I feel stupid every time I look at it.

alts.text: You know that fancy blender I was all excited about? Used it twice. It's so loud I can't make anything before everyone's up, so it just hogs half the counter and I feel dumb every time I see it.

Do you remember the expensive blender I was so excited about? I have used it twice. It is so loud that I cannot make anything before everyone is awake, so now it simply occupies half the counter, and I feel foolish every time I look at it.

sentences.note: **takes up half the counter** 는 조리대 반을 차지한다는 뜻으로, 자리만 차지할 때 **take up** 을 씁니다. casual 의 **hogs** 는 혼자 독차지한다는 느낌입니다.

sentences.ko: 요즘 잠을 잘 못 자. 잠드는 건 괜찮은데 새벽 3시에 깨서 회사 일 생각을 하기 시작해. 그러다 마음이 좀 가라앉을 때쯤이면 어차피 일어날 시간이 다 돼 있어.
sentences.text: I haven't been sleeping well lately. I fall asleep fine, but then I wake up at three and start thinking about work, and by the time I calm down it's almost time to get up anyway.

alts.text: Sleep's been rough lately. Falling asleep's no problem, but then I'm up at three thinking about work, and by the time I calm down it's pretty much time to get up anyway.

I have not been sleeping well recently. I fall asleep without difficulty, but then I wake at three and begin thinking about work, and by the time I have calmed down, it is nearly time to get up in any case.

sentences.note: **by the time** 은 ~할 때쯤이면 이라는 뜻입니다. 문장 끝의 **anyway** 는 어차피라는 느낌을 더해 줍니다.

sentences.ko: 안녕하세요, 2B호인데요, 또 연락드려요. 난방이 아직도 안 돼요. 벌써 일주일 다 돼 가요. 사람 보내 주신다고 하셨는데 아무도 안 왔어요. 그냥 수리 기사님 번호 주시면 제가 직접 전화할게요.
sentences.text: Hi, it's me from 2B again. The heat's still not working, and it's been almost a week now. I know you said someone would come by, but nobody's shown up, so can you just give me the repair guy's number and I'll call him myself?

alts.text: Hey, 2B again. Heat's still out, and it's been almost a week. You said someone'd swing by, but nobody came, so could you just gimme the repair guy's number and I'll call him myself?

Hello, this is the tenant in 2B again. The heating is still not working, and it has now been almost a week. I understand you said someone would come by, but no one has arrived, so could you please give me the repair technician's number so that I can contact him myself?

sentences.note: **come by** 는 잠깐 들르다라는 뜻이고, **shown up** 은 나타나다, 오다입니다. **The heat's still not working** 처럼 난방은 heat 라고 간단히 말합니다.
sentences.situation: 집주인이랑 고장 난 것 고쳐 달라고 얘기하기

reviewed: 4번 formal 의 regardless 는 이 자리에서 딱딱하고 어색해서 anyway 의 뜻인 in any case 로 바꿈
2번 formal 의 frankly 는 망설이는 말투인 I don't know 와 결이 달라서 to be honest 로 바꿈
